image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standalone single-storey FamilyMart convenience store building, detailed front elevation with full-width glass frontage and sliding doors under a deep white fascia band carrying the FamilyMart wordmark and its blue and green rounded stripe device, backlit lightbox sign and slim canopy edge, shelving and a magazine rack faintly visible behind the glass, plain rendered side and rear walls with a service door and a small high window, flat roof with a low parapet and roof-mounted air-conditioning condensers Materials: white powder-coated aluminium and plate glass at the front, glossy printed lightbox vinyl, flat painted render on side and rear walls, galvanised roof plant.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow. Apart from the building's own signage described above, there is no other text or lettering anywhere in the frame.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Real trademark: FamilyMart. The repo's MIT licence covers this asset's code, not the mark; anyone shipping it needs their own trademark clearance.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93 -- not a pass self-score. 804/16000 triangles, 10/12 draw calls, 8/8 materials, 10/16 unique geometries, 2 textures. The shopfront correction made the prop CHEAPER: deleting the invented door surround took its InstancedMesh with it, and folding the four intermediate mullions into the one system that remained left ten draw calls and ten geometries against eleven of each. Materials stay at the ceiling of 8, and the decal band is what put them there -- one white material carrying two brand colours as per-box vertex colours instead of two materials.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 8.00 x 5.20 x 7.00 m against the declared 8 x 5.2 x 7, measured off the module: x +-4.000 at the parapet, y 5.200 at the coping, z -3.500 at the rear upstand and +3.500 at the fascia face. FOURTH BUILD (2026-09-03): the module raised 0.60 m on the owner's brief so the fascia field is 0.81 m (was 0.51) and the coping sits 0.42 m above the panel drip (was 0.13); everything below 3.40 m is unchanged.
featureReviews.notes: Every height in the stack is measured, not estimated: the front elevation was rectified by homography over X -4.00..+4.00 by Y 0..4.395 at 200 px/m and the +X side over Z +3.50..-3.50, both anchored on the coping landing at the declared 4.60 (95.5 px/m in the x=610 column). That gave fascia 3.40..4.47, blue trim 3.47..3.59, green band 4.10..4.39 -- now 3.40..4.78 / 3.47..3.59 / 4.40..4.72 at the same ratios -- shopfront head 3.36, kick rail 0.05..0.25 and plinth 0..0.12. One correction: the base line was first fitted to the silhouette's bottom, which is the contact SHADOW, and every height came out 4% tall until it was refitted to the four columns where the white kerb separates from the shadow. The roofline is unbroken -- the plate's tall louvred unit stands above its parapet and here tops out at 5.19 under the declared ceiling, recorded as a deliberate departure.

featureReviews.evidence: Green #35A24B over white #E5E6E8 over blue #2191C5 (0.32 / 0.81 / 0.12 m of a 1.38 m panel), with the mark GENERATED by nano-banana-2/edit from the plate's sign crop -- emblem and wordmark as separate calls, keyed and recoloured to the measured pair -- and laid out at the rectified plate's ratios: group 0.72 of the field tall (0.58 m), emblem 0.67 wide, gap 0.22, wordmark 2.96, the 3.86 m group centred on X 0 where the plate's centre is X -0.05. The joints moved out to +-2.45 / +-3.30 so no seam crosses it. Fascia white measured at standard deviation 1.8 over 9,660 px; the blue is the mean of the 400 most-blue pixels of the trim (#2291C6) and of the wordmark (#2090C4), which agree to one level.
featureReviews.notes: One baked WebP on TWO boards of one panel: the front face and a +X RETURN board sampling u 0.02..0.30, a stretch of the same band with no mark on it, because the plate's return carries the colours and not the logo. One correction: the parapet ring was at the template's +-4.00 and stood 0.01 m proud of the return board, hiding it outright -- the azimuth-90 frame showed a bare wall with the blue trim peeking out below the parapet's foot. The ring is now pulled in to +-3.975 and the outward stack on that elevation is wall 3.94 < parapet 3.975 < frame 3.985 < door fittings 3.995 < fascia 4.000. The third build's Liberation Sans wordmark was a fifth of the field tall and read as a label; the owner asked for a bigger centred mark and a taller building to carry it.

featureReviews.evidence: SEVEN verticals and ONE transom, counted by column scan of the rectified front in three separate height bands (Y 1.55..1.85, 2.30..2.50, 2.95..3.15 at threshold luma 130) that agree to within 0.03 m: -3.37 w0.15, -2.02 w0.065, -0.83 w0.065, +0.255 w0.125, +1.21 w0.065, +2.41 w0.070, +3.72 w0.19. SIX run sill 0.05 to head 3.36. The seventh, +0.255, is present in the 1.55 and 2.30 bands and ABSENT from the 2.95 one -- it is the sliding pair's meeting stile and it stops at the transom, which is how it is built (Y 0.10..2.60). The transom is a single 0.21 m rail at Y 2.56..2.77; a row scan of that band puts its ends at X -2.05 and +2.44, so it spans the four middle bays and dies into the mullions, leaving the left and right bays glazed full height. The sensor plate sits on it at X -0.02..+0.34, also scanned.
featureReviews.notes: Two builds got the count wrong and this is the correction. The first had no entrance at all -- five identical glazed bays and a flat pane where the door is. The second invented a PROJECTING DOOR SURROUND between X -2.02 and +1.22: 2.73 m jambs standing 0.08 m proud, its own head, a short transom mullion above that head, and a sidelight jamb -- five parts describing a frame the plate does not have, and the reason the shopfront read as a box hung on the glass. -2.02 and +1.21 are ordinary full-height mullions of the same 0.065 m section as -0.83 and +2.41. Removing the surround took a draw call and a geometry off the prop as well.

featureReviews.evidence: Mill-finish aluminium #D4D6D5 (standard deviation 11.2 on the rectified kick rail), not the MK sibling's near-black steel. Verticals at the SCANNED X -3.34, -2.02, -0.83, +0.255, +1.21, +2.41 and +3.80 -- an uneven rhythm of 1.32, 1.19, 1.09, 0.96, 1.20 and 1.39 m, not a grid -- and four of the seven share one 0.065 m section and are therefore one InstancedMesh of four rather than four boxes in the merge. The shopfront TURNS THE CORNER: glazing 0.95 m and framing onto the +X wall, with the fascia returning 2.55 m. The FamilyMart green-over-blue decal band runs at Y 1.15..1.27 across the panes, both sliding leaves and the return -- eight merged boxes on ONE white material carrying per-box vertex colours, because a material per colour would have put the prop over its ceiling of 8.
featureReviews.notes: Scored below the other criticals for one reason. The plate's glazing is transparent and shows a full shop interior -- shelving, a chiller, a magazine rack, the FamilyMart decal stripe -- and none of it ships. It DID, for one build, as the plate's own shopfront rectified into the glazing plane and projected by world x/y, the same route MK uses; it was removed on review because a baked interior is a flat picture on a flat pane. It carries no parallax, so it slides against the framing as the camera orbits, and the mullions and rails printed into it argue with the ones this model builds as geometry at the same positions. The pane ships tinted at #6F7371, the darkest tone that clears the turntable gate at all four azimuths, which is also what the kit's exterior-shell rule asks for. The two homographies stay in the tree: they are what the layout above was measured from. The decal stripe went with the image and is the one identity feature this prop no longer carries.

featureReviews.evidence: Service door leaf at Z +0.78..-0.28 by Y 0..2.40 with a louvre at its foot and a lever at 1.15, and a 0.85 x 0.66 m window at Z -2.93..-2.08 -- all read off the +X rectification, all in ONE painted-steel component because the plate measures the door leaf (#3E4346) and the window glass (#3D3F3E) at the same value.
featureReviews.notes: Two corrections. The steel was first lifted 1.43x for the hole gate and at luma 146 the door rendered at 118 against a 129 wall and stopped reading as a door, where the plate has it at 0.59 of its wall; it ships at 116. And the window pane, set back 3 cm in a reveal, rendered at luma 69 at azimuth 90 -- 0.63 of its albedo where the wall beside it manages 0.88 -- and the turntable gate read the 103 x 68 px opening as background punched through the wall. Flush with its surround it clears. Deliberately NOT mirrored onto the -X wall, which the plate never shows.

featureReviews.evidence: FOUR different units in one merged galvanised component: a hooded duct run with two brackets, a wall-type condenser behind a square fan guard with a cylinder cowl, a riser box with a conduit drop, and a tall louvred tower with a louvre face and a cap.
featureReviews.notes: The first build carried ONE bank. The template's instanced condenser system is left EMPTY here, which is a legitimate answer rather than a missing config: instancing one casing three times is one draw call and so is merging four different ones, so the repetition would have cost fidelity to save nothing. Plan positions are read through a Y=4.60 homography of the roof and are the softest numbers on the prop -- the plant sits a metre below that plane -- so they are reported at 0.74 confidence.

Same footprint as the 7-Eleven store building; the blue and green livery and the taller parapet are the differences.
